question.problem: Let $F(x)=x^2+10x$ for $x\in[0,6),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **odd** extension of $F(x)$ to $x \in (-6,6).$ What is the value of $f(-1)?$
question.worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in[0,6),$ the odd extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14227643/assets/de535d3df741309e51bab7305aedcb27507b078771f0931d4914e16c88220926.svg)

In our case, for $x\in(-6,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-F(-x) \\  & =-((-x)^{2}+10(-x)) \\  & =-({x}^{2}-10x) \\  & =-{x}^{2}+10x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) & =-(-1)^{2}+10(-1)=-11.\end{aligned}
$$
